title: Air Force hunts for Scientist X

tellings.quote: Two hours after the lecture ended, Air Force investigators had shown up and were questioning students for clues about Scientist X's identity.

plain: In Denver in 1950, Michels says, a lecture was given about crashed flying saucers, tied to an anonymous figure known only as "Scientist X", and two hours after it ended Air Force investigators were questioning students for clues to who Scientist X really was. Michels tells it himself and names people called Hansen, Unger and George Kohler among the figures in the story. If true, it would mean the Air Force took the lecture seriously enough to hunt down its source right away.
